marta: Heads-up — perf run on the TP matrix (8-way TP across 4 nodes) shows a clear regression when KV-cache churn creates lots of tiny all-reduces. Profiling attached below.

marta: TL;DR: ring vs tree shapes flip cost at ~64KB messages. For <64KB tree path with fragmentation + kernel selection overhead ends up slower than a tuned ring. Expected opposite.

marta: Quick snippet from perf: 
```
# timeline (micro-bench)
allreduce_size=32KB latency=1.8ms shape=tree
allreduce_size=48KB latency=2.1ms shape=tree
allreduce_size=80KB latency=2.3ms shape=ring
allreduce_size=128KB latency=2.6ms shape=ring
```

marta: Kernel selector is picking fused-reduce kernel for tree that has high launch overhead for small fragments. Also NVLink saturation pattern looks odd — packets are many small payloads.

ajay: ugh. Is this the same workload where KV cache writes are per-token? If cache flushes on every generation step we could be seeing lots of small key updates.

marta: Exactly. KV cache delta sends are ~12-48KB depending on prompt, so we get many all-reduces of small sizes.

xiang: Two quick thoughts: 1) coalesce KV writes client-side (batch per request window) 2) runtime-level heuristic: prefer ring for message sizes in [16KB..96KB] when kernel-launch-cost > threshold.

denise: Do we have numbers for kernel launch overhead and host->device enqueue times? Might be kernel launch + soft-affinity causing the cost.

marta: Collected wall times from our tracer: 
```
kernel_launch_overhead=80-120us
fragment_copy_host2dev=40-90us
nccl_call_enqueue=30-50us
```

marta: So when each fragment is small, overhead dominates.

ajay: I pushed a quick patch to runtime chunker to align frag sizes to 64KB boundaries instead of 16KB. Bench locally — reduced call count by ~3x. Patch: 
```
# patch pseudocode
frag = round_up(size, 65536)
```

ajay: Results after patch (local sim): 
```
allreduce_size=64KB latency=1.2ms shape=ring
allreduce_size=128KB latency=1.9ms shape=ring
```

xiang: Nice. Can you post the branch? I want to run on multi-node.

ajay: branch: feat/tp-chunk-align-64k — run against staging cluster 3 tonight.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled to staging: feat/tp-chunk-align-64k at 23:10 UTC — 3 nodes (gpu-rt-*)

marta: Also experimenting with an NCCL tweak: forcing algorithm selection override for small messages. Try `NCCL_ALGO=RING` vs `TREE` and `NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=2`. In our env ring seems to win for mid-small sizes.

xiang: Note: tree benefits when you have hierarchical cross-node links (switch with IB fat-tree). But our topology is mixed and NVSwitch+B daisy chain gives ring better burst characteristics for small payloads.

denise: Could we add a profiler metric: "small_allreduce_ratio" (percent of allreduce calls < 64KB) per model route? Would help correlate regressions to KV churn.

marta: Good idea. Logged RFC in the perf dashboard.

ajay: After running on staging i see ~25% latency improvement for the generation path with high KV churn when enabling chunk-align and forcing ring via env var.

marta: Two follow-ups: 1) runtime heuristic (align/fragments + prefer ring in that size window) 2) client-side coalescing for KV writes + X docs on recommended prompt batching.

xiang: I'll take heuristic task. Will add a configurable threshold and an override flag for topology exceptions.

denise: I'll add the small_allreduce_ratio to the route-level metrics and dashboard.

marta: Assigning owners: @xiang for runtime heuristic (PR review ping when ready), @denise for metric/dashboard, @ajay to own client coalescing RFC + perf run notes.

ops-bot: Reminder: please update the perf-regressions board with the staging run IDs and attach results.

marta: Will drop the staging logs and perf flame graphs here after runs complete. Thanks all :rocket: 

marta: FYI — repro command used: 
```
./run_tp_microbench --tp=8 --nodes=4 --kv-churn=high --cache-mode=delta
```
